messages.content: The organizer moved the first required meeting to 8:45 Thursday morning, so I’m not comfortable with the same-day flight anymore. Compare the Wednesday evening option with a few hotels near the office and show me the real total.
I’ll use the unbooked 7:10 p.m. Wednesday departure from O’Hare, arriving Minneapolis at 8:42 p.m., and compare it with refundable downtown rooms. What office address should I measure the walks from?
80 South Eighth Street. The hotel reimbursement limit is $300 including tax, and this is only for Wednesday night.

Three refundable options fit that limit for May 13. The Marquette Hotel is about a 4-minute walk from the office at $286 including tax. Hampton Inn & Suites Minneapolis/Downtown is about 11 minutes away at $246 including tax. Hilton Garden Inn Minneapolis Downtown is about 13 minutes away at $259 including tax. All are standard king rooms at the current quoted rates.
How practical is the 8:42 arrival? I don’t want the posted landing time treated as the hotel arrival time.

With an on-time arrival, allow about 15 minutes to exit the aircraft and reach the terminal light-rail station. The Blue Line takes roughly 25 minutes to Nicollet Mall, followed by a 6- to 12-minute walk depending on the hotel. A realistic hotel arrival is 9:35 to 9:50 p.m. A rideshare would usually put you downtown around 9:25 to 9:40 p.m., but traffic and pickup time can erase much of the advantage.
Give me the cancellation cutoff for each hotel, not just that they’re refundable.

The Marquette can be canceled without penalty until 11:59 p.m. local time on May 12; after that, the charge is one night plus tax. Hampton allows free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. local time on May 12, then charges one night plus tax. Hilton Garden Inn allows free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. local time on May 11, with a one-night-plus-tax penalty afterward.
The Hilton doesn’t seem to earn its extra cost. Compare Marquette and Hampton against the same-day plan we had.

Using light rail in both directions at an estimated $5 total, the original same-day plan would have been $402: $397 airfare plus $5 local transit. The Wednesday-night plan with the Marquette is $620: $329 airfare, $286 hotel, and $5 transit. With Hampton it is $580: $329 airfare, $246 hotel, and $5 transit. Hampton adds $178 over the same-day plan; the Marquette adds $218.
And the flight price still includes the 6:20 Thursday return?

Yes. The $329 airfare pairs the Wednesday 7:10-8:42 p.m. ORD-MSP nonstop with the Thursday 6:20-7:52 p.m. MSP-ORD nonstop. It is a standard economy fare, nonrefundable but changeable without a change fee; any fare difference would apply.
What does the extra $40 for the Marquette actually buy me besides a shorter number on the walk?

It saves about seven minutes each way on foot and keeps you connected to the office area through the downtown skyway network during its operating hours. For this stay, that mainly improves the Thursday morning commute. Hampton is still straightforward: about an 11-minute outdoor walk, or somewhat longer using available skyway segments. Both should get you to the office comfortably before 8:45.
Then Hampton is the better value. Now check the returns after 4:00 because the organizer still hasn’t told me exactly when we finish.

There are three relevant nonstop returns. A 5:05 p.m. departure arrives O’Hare at 6:37 p.m. and makes the combined airfare $312. The existing 6:20 p.m. departure arrives at 7:52 p.m. and keeps airfare at $329. A 7:35 p.m. departure arrives at 9:07 p.m. and makes airfare $346. All three are currently the same nonrefundable, changeable economy fare type.
They’ve only narrowed the meeting end to somewhere between 3:45 and 4:30. Assess those flights from the office, including getting my bag from the hotel.

The 5:05 flight is not workable even with a 3:45 finish. For the 6:20 flight, a 3:45 finish allows time to walk to Hampton, collect the bag, take the Blue Line, and reach the terminal around 5:10 to 5:25. A 4:30 finish compresses terminal arrival to roughly 5:55 to 6:10, so that flight becomes too risky. The 7:35 departure remains practical with either ending time, with an estimated terminal arrival around 5:55 to 6:10 after a 4:30 finish.
Could I leave the bag somewhere closer to the office Thursday, or does that create more trouble than it saves?

The Marquette would reduce the bag-retrieval detour because it is only about four minutes from the office, but switching hotels adds $40. Even then, a 4:30 meeting end would leave the 6:20 flight with little margin. Hampton plus the 7:35 return is both less expensive overall and more robust than paying for the Marquette to chase the earlier flight.
Show me the two sensible complete combinations. One for an early finish and one if it runs to 4:30.

Early-finish combination: Wednesday 7:10-8:42 p.m. ORD-MSP, Hampton at $246 including tax, and Thursday 6:20-7:52 p.m. MSP-ORD. Airfare is $329; with $5 light rail, total trip cost is $580. The hotel is cancelable without penalty until 6:00 p.m. May 12.

Late-finish combination: the same Wednesday outbound and Hampton stay, then Thursday 7:35-9:07 p.m. MSP-ORD. Airfare is $346; with hotel and light rail, total trip cost is $597. The same hotel cancellation terms apply.
How early would I need the organizer to confirm the ending time without risking a price or cancellation problem?

The useful decision deadline is 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, May 12, when Hampton’s free-cancellation window closes. Flight prices can change before then, so confirming earlier would reduce fare risk, but neither flight is being held. If the organizer confirms a 3:45 finish, the $580 combination is reasonable. If the end remains 4:30 or uncertain, the $597 combination is the safer choice.
Keep those two combinations and don’t book anything yet. I’ll finalize as soon as the organizer gives me the Thursday ending time.

Nothing has been booked. I’ll retain both complete plans: the $580 option with Hampton and the 6:20 p.m. return for a confirmed early finish, and the $597 option with Hampton and the 7:35 p.m. return if the meeting ends at 4:30 or remains uncertain. Both use the Wednesday 7:10 p.m. outbound, and the hotel’s free-cancellation cutoff is 6:00 p.m. local time on May 12.
